item.title: Friends and relationships
item.description: Getting on with people, arguing and making up.

children.definition: to have a friendly relationship with someone
children.example: I get on well with my flatmates.

children.definition: to stop being friends with someone after an argument
children.example: Timur fell out with his best friend over money.

children.definition: to become friends again after an argument
children.example: They argued all morning but made up before lunch.

children.definition: to believe that someone is honest and will not hurt you
to help and encourage someone, especially when things are difficult
children.example: My family supported me when I lost my job.

children.definition: to speak angrily to someone because you disagree
to say you are sorry for something you did
knowing someone very well and liking them a lot
children.example: Malika and I have been close friends since school.

children.definition: a person you know, but not very well
children.example: He isn't really a friend, just an acquaintance from work.

children.definition: unhappy because someone has something that you want
children.example: She was jealous of her sister's new phone.

children.definition: to need someone and trust them to help you
children.example: You can always rely on Dilnoza; she never forgets a promise.

children.definition: to continue to talk or write to someone who is far away
children.example: My cousin moved to Seoul, but we keep in touch online.
